answers.answer: During London Season, roll one die simultaneously for each office card a player holds. Add one to that office’s roll for each fatigue on its card; the Chairman also adds one. A modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue to the card, and 5 or higher retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return that card’s fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make these normal attrition rolls.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with the most total windows, counting newly acquired prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards as players select or discard; if the display empties, skip every remaining eligible player immediately. After selection, discard all remaining display cards and refill to exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody selected a card. Return all unused pensioners to their supplies.
evidence: I. London Season — Retirements and Prestige

answers.answer: At the start of the Family phase, each player checks which action their opportunity marker matched at phase start. They choose a main action once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched that action, then move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; that action is never doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the player may take Enlist Writer twice, and the four-vacancy bonus adds one writer once that turn, for three writers total.
evidence: II. Family — action sequence and Enlist Writer

answers.answer: After all Family actions, while both Debt and Stock Exchange applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Court pieces are Company shares. Once Debt is zero, slide any remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The purchase money for Seek Share was paid to the bank at the queue space’s printed cost; it never went into Company treasuries.
evidence: II. Family — Seek Share; New Company shares

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order by the number on each office card’s back. The designated hirer chooses a candidate, who moves into the office, and that candidate’s family gets the office card. For an ordinary office hire into your own family, obtain verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from this Nepotism consent rule. When promoting an officeholder, transfer that office’s fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no eligible candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman first announces how many shares are required for a pure majority, meaning more than half of the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that number of shares wins. Move one of the winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If no candidate gets the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority calculations and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a family member from supply or, if necessary and possible, taking one from a prize and losing that prize’s VP; if this is impossible, there is no Chairman.

For a Company-office success check, first commit the resources and cash; all cash for the check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice to trigger possible officer losses.

The Chairman may add up to three Debt without consent, receiving £5 Balance for each advance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and Debt may never pass the end of its track. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved as long as the total borrowing follows these limits; money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.

The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships remain only until Refresh.

The President chooses when its own Trade occurs relative to its Commander and Governors, but must give each position an opportunity; a position may decline, and one position must finish before the next begins. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order but cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases. For Trade, declare the home region and only regions reachable from it through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the Presidency treasury buys one die, and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failed attempt may be retried if affordable; retries belong to that President’s uninterrupted opportunity, so another position cannot act between them. A President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President’s home region even if that office is vacant. Add each order’s printed value to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; the President gets £1 from the bank per order and each writer owner gets £1 per writer placed.

A Commander may Deploy against a region in its own Presidency’s home, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. It cannot target another Presidency’s home or a Company-controlled region belonging to another Presidency. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust selected officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses. A noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources.

On a successful Deploy, loot taken from the bank is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the surviving officers used in that attempt plus one. Count only surviving participating officers and the regiments and alliances used in that attempt. Distribute each payout cycle in this order: £1 for the Commander plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer of each other family clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until the loot is spent. The Commander also gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags; open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not already Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President’s box, put the Governor overlay on the conquered region, and send only the Governor office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring. Do not create Governors/overlays if a Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in the conquered region facing outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and returns to supply; exhausted officers still roll for losses, and there is no successful-control procedure.
evidence: Actions — Commanders and Deploy; Successful control procedure

answers.answer: A Governor takes the printed dice pool and may make repeated Administer attempts. Each attempt rolls the current pool without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one benefit: Build a Company ship, Commission a regiment, or Tax. A ship requires two successful Build actions: if there is no partially built ship in the region, place one there; otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President. A commissioned regiment goes into that President’s Army, has officer-like strength, pays loot to the bank, and causes no officer-loss rolls. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury; each Tax after the first that turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.

During Company expenses, reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one step per loan until the Debt track ends. Continue receiving loans even at maximum Debt. Emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After taking emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two spaces. Then compare the remaining Balance to the expectations for current Standing; if it is below expectations, lower Standing one. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, each costing one cash per Company share and paying each share owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
evidence: VI. Revenue — Company expenses, expectations, dividends

answers.answer: A Crisis is resolved at the Elephant’s location, with its tail as attacker and head as target, then the Elephant marches. For an Invasion Crisis, compare the sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against the defender’s whole empire strength; success requires strictly greater strength. On failure, the attacker loses one tower. For a Rebellion Crisis, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength; other empire regions do not count, and success also requires strictly greater strength. On failure, remove one tower from the capital. For an attack on a Company region, resolve secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest after the primary attack; their order is primary first, then Bombay, Madras, Bengal, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Invasion/Rebellion attack strength is its ordinary strength plus unrest in the target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, without added unrest. A secondary Rebellion’s strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region, without event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling that attack strength or as much as possible, using local alliances at printed strength and not splitting them. If newly exhausted defense is insufficient, apply Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that attacked region and give the Commander one trophy; if this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the primary Invasion succeeds against the Company, apply empire growth. When the Commander position is vacant, Military Affairs acts in its stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains or loses no trophies.
evidence: VII. Events in India — Crisis; Attacks on Company; Region Loss

answers.answer: The Prime Minister reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one, and discards the others; drawing a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing. The PM chooses direction around the dial and stops on the first policy space matching the law’s bottom icon, chooses its target and consequence, reads the law, and sets Vote to its printed starting support. Voting starts with the PM and proceeds clockwise; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes, with used cards rotated. Players may adjust support up or down. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. A player may switch from supporting to opposing during this vote, but after opposing cannot support it. Track opposition votes; the biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, with the current holder retaining it on a tie. With the recipient’s consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose and count toward their opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced by the “Vote with my enterprises” promise. At support −1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma’s If Failed text, the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial, and the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher, it passes: place it among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first and then the law’s immediate effects. Restore every used voting card to its regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
evidence: VIII. Parliament Meets — Voting and Resolution

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. The ordinary voting procedure and support threshold apply, with these exceptions: Deregulation has no policy, the PM may vote against it, and failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law. If it passes, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. The 1813 scenario begins deregulated.

After Family share creation and before Hiring, players may take firm investment actions in any order until no one wishes to act; firm managers resolve timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms. A player may form a firm only if they currently manage none: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set value to the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in a firm, get its manager’s consent and contribute a Company share or workshop, creating a firm share and placing £5 from the bank in London. A firm can have at most ten shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. The Chairman share cannot be used; a Company share cannot be invested when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and shares created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested, including after firm failure, and give neither workshop bonus nor Company-failure VP. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries except through specified procedures.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port, requiring at least one ship, and commit a secret cash bid from London, or choose Hobnob, which has no bid, trade, or dividends but still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker. A closed home port is allowed when choosing the strategy. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency’s operations, before any actions, reveal matching strategies and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. The President’s successful Trade sets its initiative the same way. After that success, fill orders in ascending initiative; the President chooses ties, so the Company does not automatically go first. If the President is vacant or does not successfully trade, firms fill after the Commander and Governors have had their opportunity, with the Chairman choosing initiative ties. A firm fills as many open orders as possible up to ships plus one, beginning at its selected home port and tracing a connected route back there; it can fill any particular order only once. Place filled tokens and pay revenue to the firm’s India treasury. Firms may refill orders filled by others this turn, and the Company may refill firm orders; a previously filled order pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for every full £6 added to its India treasury that turn.
evidence: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, firms pay expenses before the Company, in initiative order, then other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows, then PM clockwise order. Pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm’s share count or firm value, using either or both firm treasuries. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from the India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with the manager’s consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid, not the per-share amount, as the dividend marker. An active firm other than a Hobnob firm that pays none records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. If the firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops remain invested. Rescue options are emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop rules—even if the ten-share cap prevents more shares—which pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment; or merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
evidence: Deregulation — Firm expenses, rescue and dividends
